reviews.summary: The set-up list, the 8pm/1pm sample line and the time-difference table work, but the People-also-ask question on fun websites for couples to play online had no direct answer, and 'holiday' and 'leave' in the 777 answer are UK words.

Every template and game claim checked out against the code, but 'our free couple games play from two phones' overstated it (only know, rather and draw do, src/lib/games/catalogue.ts), and 'holiday', 'leave' and 'post them' are UK usage.

The energy sorting and time-zone table beat the top listicles, but the post left out the watch-party sync tool and the virtual escape room the AI overview leads with, never answered the 'fun websites for couples' question directly, and didn't link the /long-distance hub whose clock tool shows the hours you're both awake.

reviews.summary: Both fixes made. It sorts dates by the energy you have tonight and gives the set-up that makes a call a date, a line to copy and a time-difference table, where the top results pile up interchangeable ideas.

Every claim checks out against the code and the tools named, the energy-sorted dates come with a time-zone table whose arithmetic holds, and both languages read like a friend who has done this, which the generic listicles on page one don't.

The only page sorted by the energy you have that night, with a set-up checklist, a line to send, a time-difference table and free games that work from two phones; the ranking pages are longer lists of the same ideas with no how-to.
